When we are comparing only two people or things, it is possible to use the word "the" in front of a comparative adjective instead of using a superlative adjective. For example, "I have two bedrooms in my flat. The smaller of the two is used as a storeroom.".
Give me an example of the word "the" used in front of a comparative adjective instead of a superlative adjective.
Of the two restaurants on this street, this one is the more expensive.
Give me an example of the word "comparatively", please.
For a lady of 92, her hearing is comparatively good.
cut back

The word "economic" means "related to money or the economy". For example, we can say "The country is facing severe economic challenges". The word "economical", on the other hand, means "providing good value" or "requiring less money than usual". For example, we can say "The car cost quite a lot to buy, but it's very economical to run".

What does the verb "flatter" mean?
The verb "flatter" means to praise someone or pay them compliments to make them feel good about themselves.
